Abstract.AbstractText: Lack of blood flow and aberrant levels of oxygenation in placentas are recurrent in pregnancy diseases, such as preeclampsia. These alterations generate situations of hypoxia and hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) and consequent oxidative stress, increased cell death, and inflammation in trophoblasts. The models used to understand the effects of hypoxia and H/R on trophoblasts require a rather big structure. This chapter describes the details of a suitable and reasonable approach with hypoxia chambers to expose human placental trophoblasts to variable conditions of oxygenation.
